t: You're on Regent Street, where Hanover Chapel once stood. It was a church, built in 1825 and demolished in 1896, so it's no longer here to see. It was designed by Charles Robert Cockerell, an English architect, archaeologist and writer. He spent seven years on a Grand Tour, mainly in Greece, before setting up a successful practice in London. He later served as Professor of Architecture at the Royal Academy, and in 1848 became the first recipient of the Royal Gold Medal.
